answer: An agent marketplace requires each voting identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days, with equal voting weight per bond. The public registry serves as a lantern for auditing deposits, while locked capital provides an anchor for each vote. Creating 10,000 identities therefore ties up $1 million; splitting the same funds across more names buys no extra votes. The market offers no haven for costless identities, though wealthy attackers can still purchase influence.
